players.product: regulated transmission & distribution utilities (ComEd, PECO, BGE, PHI) interconnecting data-center load in PJM

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (CEO Calvin G. Butler / CFO Jeanne M. Jones): adjusted operating earnings of $2.77 per share for 2025 ($2.73 on a GAAP basis), above guidance, helped mainly by favorable weather and storm conditions and the resolution of certain regulatory proceedings. Q4 earnings were $0.59 per share non-GAAP ($0.58 GAAP). The CEO said Exelon has grown earnings 7.4% a year since 2021 and grew rate base 8% in 2025. It has beaten the midpoint of guidance every year as a standalone utility.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 adjusted operating EPS $2.77 ($2.73 GAAP); Q4 $0.59 non-GAAP ($0.58 GAAP); 7.4% annual earnings growth since 2021; 8% rate base growth in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Exelon initiated 2026 operating earnings guidance of $2.81 to $2.91 per share, aiming for the midpoint or better. The CFO said the implied midpoint is ahead of previous disclosures, with midpoint-to-midpoint growth above 6%. She expects Q1 at approximately 31% of the full-year midpoint. Annualized earnings growth is projected near the top end of 5% to 7% from the 2025 guidance midpoint of $2.69 per share through 2029, on 7.9% rate base growth and earned ROEs of 9% to 10%. Asked how the plan reaches the top end despite financing drag, the CFO pointed to AFUDC on the growing transmission capital. Dividend growth stays at 5% a year, with $1.68 per share expected in 2026. On costs, management cited about $580 million of annual O&M savings versus inflation-level growth and nearly flat expenses from 2024 to 2026, and it targets no more than 2.5% adjusted O&M growth through 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 guidance $2.81 to $2.91 per share (midpoint-to-midpoint growth above 6%); Q1 approximately 31% of midpoint; near top end of 5% to 7% annualized growth through 2029; 2026 dividend $1.68 per share

quarterly_data.signal: Four-year capital plan through 2029: $41.3 billion, almost $10 billion of it in 2026. That is an increase of $3.3 billion or 9% over the prior plan. The CFO said approximately 70% of the increase, or $2.3 billion, is incremental transmission investment. She tied it to demand for high-voltage investment and capacity expansion for large load growth, evolving generation supply, and weather resiliency. A majority of the added transmission is system performance and capacity expansion that supports incremental data center load, alongside gradual replacement of an aging network. The plan adds another year of spend on the two largest transmission projects, Brandon Shores and Tri County (in service 2028 through 2030), plus early spend on the MISO Tranche 2.1 project (in service 2034). Annualized rate base growth is 7.9%, adding nearly $23 billion of rate base from 2025 to 2029. The CEO said the plan spans seven regulatory jurisdictions including FERC, with no jurisdiction above 30% and no single project above 3% of the plan. The CFO said Exelon has executed within 2% of its capital plan since 2023.
quarterly_data.figure: $41.3 billion four-year capital plan (up $3.3 billion or 9%); almost $10 billion in 2026; approximately 70%, or $2.3 billion, of the increase is transmission; 7.9% annualized rate base growth; nearly $23 billion rate base added from 2025 to 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Transmission growth and data-center-backed upside: the CFO said Exelon's size, reliability and expertise in owning and operating 765 kV lines let it grow transmission rate base at a CAGR of over 15% from 2025 through the end of the guidance period. She said Exelon now has line of sight to an additional $12 billion to $17 billion of transmission opportunities over the next decade. Over 60% of that involves projects tied to existing infrastructure. The upside includes an estimated $1 billion of transmission-associated high-density load projects with signed transmission security agreements (TSAs), which she called a foundation for more certainty in the pipeline. The agreements are presented to customers coming out of Exelon's cluster study process. She added that meeting Illinois CEJA goals amid economic development will likely require billions in transmission investments.
quarterly_data.figure: transmission rate base CAGR over 15% from 2025 through the guidance period; an estimated $1 billion of transmission-associated high-density load projects with signed TSAs within $12 billion to $17 billion of transmission opportunities over the next decade (over 60% tied to existing infrastructure)

quarterly_data.signal: Competitive transmission wins: the CEO said PJM's recent reliability window recommended $1.2 billion of incremental Exelon investment, including a jointly developed solution with NextEra. This follows other large transmission awards: Brandon Shores, Tri County and the MISO Tranche 2.1 project. The CFO said MISO Tranche 2.1 carries over $1 billion of investment in the ComEd service territory and is now getting a cost allocation filing at FERC. Management said Exelon will stay active in future PJM and other ISO windows and pursue competitive projects inside and outside PJM. (The NextEra mention is a joint transmission project, not a supply or customer relationship, so no edge was added.)
quarterly_data.figure: $1.2 billion of incremental Exelon investment recommended in the PJM reliability window; over $1 billion of MISO Tranche 2.1 investment in the ComEd service territory

quarterly_data.signal: Demand: the CEO said Exelon sees robust demand in its jurisdictions, with anticipated load growth exceeding 3% through 2029. He said the large load pipeline is further supported by an increasing number of signed transmission security agreements (TSAs). The CFO described Exelon's "first-of-its-kind transmission security agreements filed at FERC" as a clear path to interconnection for large loads that also protects existing customers. The CEO said Exelon advanced TSAs that prioritize large loads while keeping existing customers protected.

PJM supply stress and utility-generation push: during Winter Storm FERN, the PJM RTO had five straight days of peak load between 135 and 140 gigawatts, 97% of the all-time winter peak. Fewer than 1% of Exelon customers lost power. The CEO said the supply challenge is real, and he wants an all-of-the-above answer that includes utility-generated, demand-side and merchant solutions. He cited a Charles River Associates study (management said Exelon enlisted CRA's support): utility-generated power could have saved PJM customers $9.6 to $20 billion in the 2028–2029 delivery year and cut the risk of outages from energy shortages by approximately 85%. Exelon supports PJM's reliability backstop option, backs extending the PJM capacity auction collar, and joined Governor Shapiro's FERC filing. On data-center colocation, Exelon's Colette Honorable (named by the CEO on the call) said "Colocation can be a great solution" and that Exelon took its colocation stance to protect affordability. The CFO said new generation must be built at the right price.
quarterly_data.figure: PJM peak load 135 to 140 gigawatts for five days in Winter Storm FERN (97% of the all-time winter peak); utility-generated power could have saved PJM customers $9.6 to $20 billion in the 2028–2029 delivery year

quarterly_data.signal: Funding plan: the CFO expects to fund the $41.3 billion capital plan through 2029 with $22 billion of internally generated cash flow, $13 billion of utility debt and $3 billion of holding company debt, with a modest amount of equity for the rest. Incremental capital is funded approximately 40% with equity. In December the holding company issued $1 billion of convertible debt, pulling forward over half of its planned 2026 long-term corporate debt. Exelon priced $700 million of equity in 2025 through forward contracts under its ATM. Average credit metrics ended 2025 at 13.5%, against a 12% Moody's downgrade threshold. The target is 14% over the planning period, which gives 100 to 200 basis points of cushion above the downgrade thresholds.
quarterly_data.figure: $22 billion internal cash flow, $13 billion utility debt, $3 billion holding company debt; $1 billion convertible debt issued in December; $700 million of equity priced in 2025; credit metrics 13.5% vs 12% downgrade threshold, 14% target

quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory calendar: on January 16, ComEd filed its multiyear grid plan for 2028–2031, with a final order expected in December and its next rate filing in 2027. Pepco Maryland base rate case: final order expected in August. In December, Delmarva Power filed a Delaware electric base rate case seeking a net revenue increase of $44.6 million, with interim rates expected July 9. BGE will file probably in the first half, since its rates expire in 2027, and Exelon is still weighing its approach in Pennsylvania. Earlier, Atlantic City Electric settled at a 9.6% ROE and Exelon received about half of the BGE reconciliation and realigned capital accordingly. The CFO said Exelon's earned ROE has averaged around 9.4% since separation (2022 to 2025) and should hold or improve as the mix shifts toward transmission. COO Michael A. Innocenzo called New Jersey's new executive orders very constructive.
quarterly_data.figure: ComEd multiyear grid plan (2028–2031) filed January 16, final order expected in December; Delmarva Power Delaware electric rate case $44.6 million; earned ROE around 9.4% (2022 to 2025)
